html:
The Mount Tabor Indian Community is a group in Rusk County, east Texas, that claims descent from a 19th century community of the same name. The map shows it in 1492, but it is a much later community.

The historical Mount Tabor community grew from Cherokee, Creek and other families who stayed in east Texas after the Texas Cherokees were driven out in 1839, the same decade as the Trail of Tears. The modern organization was set up in 2015. Its claims to Native American heritage and continuity are disputed, including by the federally recognized Cherokee tribes. The region was earlier home to the Caddo.
